chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Hammad ibn, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The prayer is disliked in the dyed garment that is deeply saturated and dark.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer (Salat), the ritual act of worship.
key_terms.الْمَصْبُوغِ: Dyed, referring to clothing treated with colorant.
key_terms.الْمُشْبَعِ: Saturated/Deep, referring to the intensity of the dye color.
key_terms.الْمُفْدَمِ: Dark/Deep-colored, specifically referring to a dark or blackish hue.
key_terms.تُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh), a legal ruling indicating preference for avoidance but not prohibition.

ai.seo_question: What type of dyed clothing makes prayer disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies that prayer is disliked (karahah) in garments dyed with a 'deep, saturated, and dark' color, reflecting the Shia emphasis on modesty and avoiding ostentatious display during worship. Scholars interpret these descriptors as indicating a richness or intensity of color that might distract from humility, aligning with the broader principle of avoiding extravagance in religious attire.
